title: Grading white bean for sale; quality, impurities, and weight loss
excerpt: Grading white bean based on visual defects, the impact of rainfall during harvest on kernel color, and post-harvest storage principles, based on international trade standards.
content_html:
Commercial classes of dry beans

In recognized international trade standards, dry beans are divided into various classes.Academic sourceSmall white bean is defined as one of these classes. This classification is purely a commercial definition and does not correspond to the official product grading system in Iran.

Principles of grading based on visual defects

In existing trade systems, dry beans are primarily graded based on the extent of visual defects. Healthier products fall into higher grades, and products with more defects are placed in lower grades.Academic sourceBroken edges, crushed kernels, and physical impurities are among the most important factors examined during the grading process. This numerical system is specific to the American market and has no direct application in Iran.

The role of kernel appearance in selling value

The appearance of the bean kernel has a direct impact on the selling price. Skin damage, discoloration, or the presence of impurities can reduce the market value of the product.Academic sourceThis finding is based on the experience of American growers and is reported; the percentage of weight loss or the threshold level of damage has not been stated in the provided sources.

The impact of harvest conditions on visual quality

Rainfall at the time of harvest can cause discoloration of white bean kernels and reduce the visual quality of the product.Academic sourceThis phenomenon has been observed in the Missouri region of the United States, and Iran's climatic conditions are not necessarily similar. Therefore, harvest timing and avoiding excess moisture during collection are considered important factors in preserving the visual quality of beans.

Post-harvest care

To preserve kernel quality after harvest, two general principles are put forward: keeping seed moisture in a low range and avoiding rough mechanical handling.Academic sourceUsing conveyor belts instead of augers and avoiding dropping kernels from height onto hard surfaces are recommended methods in American sources. The numerical moisture value is mentioned only in the American source, and this point is reliable only qualitatively.

Packaging and storage

Beans, like other shelf-stable foods, are best stored in an environment free of oxygen and light.Academic sourceOxygen can cause the oil in the kernel to turn rancid, and light rapidly fades the color of the kernel. Suitable packaging containers include metal cans, Mylar bags, and glass jars for small quantities.

Post-harvest care guideline table

Qualitative factor Impact on the product Recommended action
Rainfall during harvest Kernel discoloration Prompt harvest and avoidance of moisture
High seed moisture in storage Reduced shelf life and quality Proper drying before storage
Rough mechanical handling Kernel breakage and crushing Use conveyor belts instead of augers
Light and oxygen in storage Fading of color and rancidity of oil Dark and airtight packaging

Note: All items presented in this article are extracted from U.S. trade and extension standards and do not represent the official bean grading system in Iran. Iran's climatic and market conditions are not necessarily similar to those sources.

faq.question: Does white bean have classifications in trade standards?
faq.answer: Yes, in recognized trade standards, small white bean is introduced as one of the commercial classes of dry beans. This classification pertains to U.S. USDA standards and does not correspond to the official Iranian grading system.

faq.question: What impact does rainfall during harvest have on white bean?
faq.answer: Rainfall at the time of harvest can cause discoloration of white bean kernels and reduce the visual quality of the product. This has been observed in the Missouri region of the United States, and Iran's climatic conditions are not necessarily similar.

faq.question: What post-harvest care is needed to preserve bean quality?
faq.answer: To preserve quality, seed moisture must be kept in a low range and rough mechanical handling should be avoided. Using conveyor belts instead of augers, not dropping kernels from height onto hard surfaces, and storing in dark, oxygen-free packaging are among the recommended measures.
